title: Two Loops, One Ratio
endLine: Sodium concentration reports water; sodium content sets the volume.

scenes.tts: Drink a litre of water quickly, and your plasma sodium concentration dips for a while. No sodium left your body. Sweat out a litre, and it rises, though sweat carries sodium out. Why?
scenes.narration: Drink a litre of water quickly, and your plasma sodium concentration dips for a while. No sodium left your body. Sweat out a litre, and it rises, though sweat carries sodium out. Why?
scenes.caption: Drink a litre of water quickly, and your plasma sodium concentration dips for a while. No sodium left your body. Sweat out a litre, and it rises, though sweat carries sodium out. Why?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: body water pale BLUE fill with a gentle shimmer; sodium GOLD dots; potassium PURPLE dots; the plasma sodium gauge, its needle and readings bright WHITE; the osmoreceptor neuron and its signal CYAN; vasopressin and water channels GREEN; sodium-loop sensors and hormones ORANGE. LAYOUT: LEFT 70% of the frame is one wide rectangular TANK of pale blue water filling about 70% of frame height (the body's water, schematic). Its WIDTH is drawn to scale in litres: the starting 42 L spans about 60% of frame width, so 1 L is about 1.4% of frame width. A dashed WHITE vertical membrane splits it 28 to 14: LEFT part labelled 'cells', full of drifting PURPLE dots; RIGHT part labelled 'outside cells', with about 70 drifting GOLD dots (5 dots per litre). Under the right part a WHITE readout 'outside: 14.0 L'. A TAP hangs above the tank. RIGHT 30%: a tall vertical gauge labelled 'plasma sodium', scale 130 to 150 (mmol per L), needle at 140, tick marks every 5. Hook motion: on 'drink a litre', the tap pours a short pale blue stream; the tank widens by 1 L, the membrane slides so the cells part takes two thirds of the new width and the outside part one third; the gold dots spread a little thinner; the gauge needle dips to about 137. On 'no sodium left', the gold dots pulse: none has gone. Quick smooth rewind to the start. On 'sweat out a litre', a small spout labelled 'sweat' opens on the right wall and drains pale blue water carrying about 2 gold dots; the tank narrows to 41 L (outside about 13.4 L), the gold dots crowd slightly, and the needle rises to about 142. On the question, white text across the top: 'Why?'

Title 'Two Loops, One Ratio' fades in over the top of the frame for 2 s while the question text fades out. The sweat spout closes and disappears for good. The tank eases back to 42 L (28 cells, 14.0 outside), the needle returns to 140. Dots keep drifting; water shimmers.

scenes.tts: Take a seventy kilogram adult with forty-two litres of body water, fourteen of them outside the cells. Cells hold their water mainly with potassium, the fluid outside mainly with sodium.
scenes.narration: Take a 70 kg adult with 42 litres of body water, 14 of them outside the cells. Cells hold their water mainly with potassium, the fluid outside mainly with sodium.
scenes.caption: Take a 70 kg adult with 42 litres of body water, 14 of them outside the cells. Cells hold their water mainly with potassium, the fluid outside mainly with sodium.
scenes.visual: Slow push-in until the tank fills about 75% of frame height; gauge stays at right. On 'forty-two litres' a WHITE bracket spans the whole tank, labelled '42 L water'. On 'fourteen litres' the 'outside: 14.0 L' readout brightens and the right part's outline glows. On 'potassium' the PURPLE dots in the cells part brighten and a label 'potassium holds' appears there; on 'sodium' the GOLD dots outside brighten and a label 'sodium holds' appears. Both labels fade at scene end. Dots keep drifting; nothing freezes.

scenes.tts: Plasma sodium sits at one hundred forty millimoles per litre: a ratio, solute over water. Water crosses cell membranes easily, so a litre you drink spreads through all forty-three litres.
scenes.narration: Plasma sodium sits at 140 mmol per litre: a ratio, solute over water. Water crosses cell membranes easily, so a litre you drink spreads through all 43 litres.
scenes.caption: Plasma sodium sits at 140 mmol per litre: a ratio, solute over water. Water crosses cell membranes easily, so a litre you drink spreads through all 43 litres.
scenes.visual: On 'one hundred forty' the gauge needle glows at 140. On 'a ratio', a large fraction builds beside the gauge: GOLD 'solute' over pale BLUE 'water', size 34; it stays on screen through s04. On 'crosses cell membranes', a few pale blue droplets pass freely back and forth through the dashed membrane in both directions. On 'a litre you drink', the tap pours a pale blue stream into the outside part; the water does not stay there: droplets flow through the membrane into the cells part, and the whole tank widens by 1 L, the membrane sliding so the cells take two thirds of the new width. The '42 L water' bracket morphs to '43 L water'.

scenes.tts: With the same solute, the concentration falls to about one hundred thirty-seven. Only about a third of a litre stays outside the cells.
scenes.narration: With the same solute, the concentration falls to about 137. Only about a third of a litre stays outside the cells.
scenes.caption: With the same solute, the concentration falls to about 137. Only about a third of a litre stays outside the cells.
scenes.visual: On 'same solute', the GOLD 'solute' term of the fraction pulses and stays the same size while the BLUE 'water' term grows a little; the gold dots outside (still about 70) spread thinner. On 'falls', the gauge needle sinks smoothly from 140 to 137, label 'about 137'. On 'a third of a litre', the outside readout counts from '14.0 L' to 'about 14.3 L' and a thin pale blue sliver at the edge of the outside part glows, labelled '+ about 0.3 L'.

scenes.tts: Sweat is far weaker than plasma. Its sodium varies widely; take fifty millimoles per litre. It removes water out of proportion to solute, so the concentration rises to about one hundred forty-two.
scenes.narration: Sweat is far weaker than plasma. Its sodium varies widely; take 50 mmol per litre. It removes water out of proportion to solute, so the concentration rises to about 142.
scenes.caption: Sweat is far weaker than plasma. Its sodium varies widely; take 50 mmol per litre. It removes water out of proportion to solute, so the concentration rises to about 142.
scenes.visual: Smooth rewind to the start (42 L, needle 140; the fraction resets). The sweat spout reappears on the right wall for this scene only. On 'far weaker than plasma', two side-by-side cups appear above the spout: 'plasma: 140' with 5 GOLD dots, and 'sweat: about 50' with 2 GOLD dots (schematic). On 'removes water', the spout drains pale blue water carrying the 2 gold dots; the tank narrows to 41 L, outside readout 'about 13.4 L'. In the fraction, the BLUE 'water' term shrinks more than the GOLD 'solute' term. On 'rises', the needle climbs to about 142, label 'about 142'. At scene end the cups and spout fade, the fraction fades, and the tank eases back to 42 L with needle at 140.

scenes.tts: A loop guards this ratio. Osmoreceptor neurons in the lamina terminalis, at the front of the brain, sense it. When plasma grows more concentrated, water leaves them, and they fire faster.
scenes.narration: A loop guards this ratio. Osmoreceptor neurons in the lamina terminalis, at the front of the brain, sense it. When plasma grows more concentrated, water leaves them, and they fire faster.
scenes.caption: A loop guards this ratio. Osmoreceptor neurons in the lamina terminalis, at the front of the brain, sense it. When plasma grows more concentrated, water leaves them, and they fire faster.
scenes.visual: The tank shifts slightly down and right to make room at top left (still about 65% of frame height). At TOP LEFT a single round CYAN neuron cartoon appears inside a simple brain outline, labelled 'osmoreceptor neuron'. A thin CYAN line connects it to the outside part of the tank (it samples the plasma). On 'more concentrated', the gauge needle nudges up to about 142 (schematic) and the gold dots crowd; pale blue droplets leave the neuron, which shrinks a little; CYAN spikes fire from it, then fire faster, as small flashes along its line.

scenes.tts: Their signal raises vasopressin. In the collecting duct, vasopressin binds V two receptors. Aquaporin two water channels move into the membrane facing the urine. Water returns to the blood.
scenes.narration: Their signal raises vasopressin. In the collecting duct, vasopressin binds V2 receptors. Aquaporin-2 water channels move into the membrane facing the urine. Water returns to the blood.
scenes.caption: Their signal raises vasopressin. In the collecting duct, vasopressin binds V2 receptors. Aquaporin-2 water channels move into the membrane facing the urine. Water returns to the blood.
scenes.visual: At BOTTOM RIGHT of the tank, a vertical COLLECTING DUCT tube appears, draining urine down out of the frame; label 'collecting duct'. On 'vasopressin', the CYAN neuron's line leads to a small node at the base of the brain outline (labelled 'pituitary') from which GREEN hormone dots stream into the outside part and drift to the duct. On 'V two receptors', GREEN dots dock on the outer (blood-facing) wall of the duct, label 'V2'. On 'aquaporin two', small GREEN vesicles inside the duct wall slide to its inner (urine-facing) side and open as GREEN pores, label 'aquaporin-2'. On 'returns to the blood', pale blue droplets leave the urine through the pores and rejoin the tank; the urine stream thins. No molecular structures: pores are simple green gaps.

scenes.tts: Without the hormone, urine can fall near fifty milliosmoles per kilogram. Short of water, it reaches about one thousand to twelve hundred. The same neurons drive thirst, which replaces water already lost.
scenes.narration: Without the hormone, urine can fall near 50 mOsm per kg. Short of water, it reaches about 1,000 to 1,200. The same neurons drive thirst, which replaces water already lost.
scenes.caption: Without the hormone, urine can fall near 50 mOsm per kg. Short of water, it reaches about 1,000 to 1,200. The same neurons drive thirst, which replaces water already lost.
scenes.visual: Beside the duct, a small vertical bar labelled 'urine (mOsm per kg)', scale 0 to 1,200. On 'without the hormone', the GREEN pores close back into vesicles, the urine stream runs wide and pale, and the bar drops to a tick at 50, label 'near 50'. On 'short of water', the pores reopen, the stream thins to a trickle, and the bar fills to a band from 1,000 to 1,200, label 'about 1,000-1,200'. On 'thirst', a CYAN line runs from the neuron to the TAP, labelled 'thirst'; on 'replaces water', the tap pours and the needle settles back to 140. The bar fades at scene end; duct, tap and neuron stay.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. In a healthy adult, plasma sodium concentration is body solute divided by body water. The water loop holds that ratio steady by adding or removing water. So the concentration reports water.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. In a healthy adult, plasma sodium concentration is body solute divided by body water. The water loop holds that ratio steady by adding or removing water. So the concentration reports water.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. In a healthy adult, plasma sodium concentration is body solute divided by body water. The water loop holds that ratio steady by adding or removing water. So the concentration reports water.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: tank, gauge, neuron, duct, tap. The 'solute over water' fraction returns beside the gauge, size 34. On 'adding', the tap pours briefly; on 'removing', the duct's urine stream widens briefly; each time the needle wobbles and returns to 140. A CYAN loop arrow draws itself from the gauge through the neuron to the tap and the duct and back, labelled 'water loop'. On 'reports water', the BLUE 'water' term of the fraction glows. The fraction fades out at scene end and does not return.

scenes.tts: Let the body keep an extra one hundred forty millimoles of sodium, about eight grams of salt. Once the water loop catches up, where does the gauge settle?
scenes.narration: Let the body keep an extra 140 mmol of sodium, about 8 g of salt. Once the water loop catches up, where does the gauge settle?
scenes.caption: Let the body keep an extra 140 mmol of sodium, about 8 g of salt. Once the water loop catches up, where does the gauge settle?
scenes.visual: On 'one hundred forty millimoles', 5 new GOLD dots (one litre's worth at 5 per litre) drop into the outside part, which stays the same width; the gold dots there crowd and the needle starts to rise. A small GOLD tag 'kept: 140 mmol' appears by them. Question card in white across the top: 'Where does the gauge settle?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the needle hovers just above 140, the five new gold dots bob, the water shimmers faintly.

scenes.tts: Back at one hundred forty. The water loop holds back water until the ratio is restored. At that strength, one hundred forty millimoles fills one litre, all outside the cells, where sodium stays.
scenes.narration: Back at 140. The water loop holds back water until the ratio is restored. At that strength, 140 mmol fills one litre, all outside the cells, where sodium stays.
scenes.caption: Back at 140. The water loop holds back water until the ratio is restored. At that strength, 140 mmol fills one litre, all outside the cells, where sodium stays.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. The needle briefly reads above 140; the CYAN neuron fires, GREEN pores open in the duct and the urine stream thins, and the tap drips. Pale blue water collects in the outside part only: the outside part widens by exactly 1 L while the cells part keeps its width (the membrane does not move). The new gold dots spread out to the same density as the rest. The needle settles at 140, label '140 again'. The outside readout counts from '14.0 L' to '15.0 L'; a bright pale blue strip of the new litre glows, labelled '+1 L'.

scenes.tts: So sodium content sets the volume outside the cells. A second loop guards it. It senses how well the arteries are filled, and sets how much sodium the kidney excretes.
scenes.narration: So sodium content sets the volume outside the cells. A second loop guards it. It senses how well the arteries are filled, and sets how much sodium the kidney excretes.
scenes.caption: So sodium content sets the volume outside the cells. A second loop guards it. It senses how well the arteries are filled, and sets how much sodium the kidney excretes.
scenes.visual: The '15.0 L' readout glows. On 'a second loop', an ORANGE ring appears on the top edge of the outside part, labelled 'artery filling', pulsing gently. On 'how much sodium the kidney excretes', an ORANGE arrow runs from it down to the duct outlet, where a small ORANGE valve controls a GOLD dot stream leaving with the urine; the arrow is labelled 'sodium loop: hormones, nerves'. The ORANGE valve opens slightly and a few gold dots leave with their water; the outside part narrows a little; the needle stays at 140 throughout. On screen: tank, gauge, neuron, duct, tap and the orange ring with its arrow, nothing more.

scenes.tts: Two loops, two quantities. Water fixes the concentration; sodium, carrying its water, fixes the volume. A low sodium reading means too much water for the solute, with body sodium low, normal or high.
scenes.narration: Two loops, two quantities. Water fixes the concentration; sodium, carrying its water, fixes the volume. A low sodium reading means too much water for the solute, with body sodium low, normal or high.
scenes.caption: Two loops, two quantities. Water fixes the concentration; sodium, carrying its water, fixes the volume. A low sodium reading means too much water for the solute, with body sodium low, normal or high.
scenes.visual: Full world. On 'water fixes the concentration', the CYAN water loop arrow and the gauge pulse together; label by the gauge 'concentration'. On 'fixes the volume', the ORANGE sodium loop arrow and the outside readout pulse together; label by the readout 'volume'. On 'too much water for the solute', the needle dips below 140 and the gold dots outside spread thinner. On 'low, normal or high', the outside part of the tank is shown narrow, then medium, then wide (three quick states of its width), the gold dots equally sparse in each and the needle low each time; tag 'low reading' by the gauge. It ends back at 15.0 L with the needle at 140.
End card over the dimmed but still moving world (dots drifting, water shimmering, needle at 140). Large white text, centred: 'Sodium concentration reports water; sodium content sets the volume.'
